description: The subject is defined against mechanism, yet the Funktionskreis -- the core analytical unit -- employs mechanistic vocabulary (receptor, effector, reflex arc). Uexkuell reinterprets but never fully escapes the machine idiom.

Uexkuell strips teleological goal-language from biology but replaces it with 'Nature's plan' -- a concept that smuggles purposiveness back in under a different name. 'Nature knows how to deal with difficulties' is itself anthropomorphic.

The Theory of Meaning oscillates between constructivism (meaning is impressed by the subject) and pre-established harmony (the Komplement-Bauplan fit implies a prior design that the subject merely activates).

The search image is simultaneously a perception image and its antagonist. Composed of the same materials (perception signs), it can erase the very perception image it resembles, making the boundary between subject-generated and stimulus-driven perception unstable.

The magical environment contradicts the stimulus-response architecture of the Funktionskreis. Early chapters build the functional cycle on perception marks from external objects; the magical chapter shows perception images arising without any object -- a free production of the subject that the original schema cannot accommodate.

Uexkuell's perspectivism declares Nature unknowable, yet the biologist who writes about tick and spider Umwelten implicitly occupies a meta-perspectival position. The reflexivity problem -- how the Umwelt theorist escapes his own Umwelt -- is never resolved.

The Kompositionslehre replaces causal explanation with contrapuntal description but never clarifies the ontological status of the meaning rule. It is not a force, not a substance, not a causal chain -- yet governs embryogenesis, cross-species adaptation, and ecological composition. Musical metaphor does real work but risks substituting analogy for explanation.

The concept of Bedeutungsduldung introduces radical passivity into a framework built on subject-constituted worlds. The fly in the spider's web and the plant being grazed are subjects whose Umwelt is violated by another subject's meaning-conferral. Active subject-constitution and passive meaning-sufferance coexist without reconciliation.

Naturtechnik promises a science of compositional principles, yet its central object -- the formative melody -- is declared inscrutable. The genes are keys, the protoplasm is material, but the melody that plays upon them is invisible. This positions Uexkuell's biology between empirical science and avowed mystery.

The anti-Darwinian stance and the Kompositionslehre share the same evidential base -- mutual organism-environment fitness -- but interpret it oppositely. Darwin sees emergent adaptation through selection; Uexkuell sees pre-composed contrapuntal harmony. The choice between them cannot be settled by the examples alone.
